While I largely enjoyed this game, as has a friend of mine I bought it for, we both came to a lot of the same conclusions. I wish there was more of a neutral review in these instances, but largely have to discourage playing it.

For the positives, the areas, humor, asthetic, and a decent chunk of the storyline is nice. It does a relatively nice job with a lot of elements, and the lumberkin are heavily worth their interactions.

For the negatives, the boss fights are poorly balanced, and start to suck the fun out of the game. Getting guilted by the developer for wanting a game to be fun and for using a save point is a very tactless, and rude thing to do that has aged poorly the farther I get into the game. The game expects a lot from the player without bringing the full level of polish it needs to accommodate or earn its right to talk smack. The developer really needs to back down off their high horse, and redesign some of the heroic and late game bosses. Numerous mechanics in general, like the Will system, almost seem interesting but wind up just further adding to the frustration of any blind player.

I can very firmly say of all the "soulslike" and "metroidvania" games I've played, this one has had the highest margin of general instabilities, the most fabricated losses lobbied against me (like exiting a save statue and randomly just straight up dying - I still have no clue how the hell that even works), and had some of the higher end ego to act like it's my problem. Some of the Heroic fights, even amongst the more hardened players I can find online, are labeled strictly RNG and regarded as annoying or poorly contrived. Further implementing excessive rewards for "no hitting" bullet hell style bosses with move spam and minion spam really makes me wonder if the developer didn't use a TAS or slow down the game rather than playing it earnestly themselves.

Get it at a discount, enjoy it until you see some of the issues I've mentioned, and put it down when it gets to be too much, or fully pass on this one. You don't have to agree, but this is my two cents. I consider this game to have a lot of unmet potential, and I'm now debating if I want to finish it, or move on to something better derived. I played a good chunk of the game and was a fan of the development team, and now I've determined I'm likely never supporting them again.

Para quem está em dúvida se vale a pena comprar o jogo, a resposta é simples: sim.

O jogo é muito bom, com uma história realmente fascinante. Ele te instiga a buscar todos os finais, tanto para completar a experiência quanto para entender melhor as diferentes possibilidades que a narrativa apresenta.

Um dos pontos mais fortes são os gráficos, especialmente impressionantes para um jogo 2D, e a trilha sonora, que tem várias músicas dignas de entrar na playlist.

Por outro lado, o combate pode parecer um pouco “duro”. Mesmo após cerca de 20 horas de jogo (no momento desta análise) e buscando todas as conquistas, ainda não me adaptei totalmente a ele. No New Game+, a situação fica mais complicada... muitos inimigos passam a dar “one-shot”, o que pode tornar a experiência frustrante. Os chefes no modo heroico seguem essa mesma linha, um erro e você morre, o que acaba deixando as batalhas um pouco monótonas.

Apesar desses pontos negativos, ainda recomendo o jogo. Ele tem seus problemas, mas seus acertos conseguem se destacar.

En 2018 jugué por primera vez a este juego, se convirtió en uno de mis favoritos, se notaba mucho el cariño al proyecto y la comunidad.

Mas tarde para 2021 salió la versión Afterlife, la cual mejoraba todo pero al mismo tiempo hacia que perdiera un poco de personalidad, si lees reseñas de cuando salió esa versión podrás ver que se añadieron zonas intermedias que antes no estaban, y sinceramente yo soy una de esas personas a las que le hubiera gustado que los añadidos fueran mas contenido extra que zonas por las que debes pasar obligatoriamente.

Dicho esto, es una joya, volví a jugar en 2026 y sinceramente mereció la pena, genuinamente si bien algunas cosas de Afterlife no me agradaron todo lo demás es una joya, es cierto que algunas cosas se sienten un poco retro, pero para mi es parte de su encanto y subjetivamente creo que es totalmente valido si no quieres jugarlo por sus mecánicas, pero si te gustan los juegos con una historia que te dejan un vacío existencial al completarlas este es uno de esos juegos, me dejo con ese vacío después de mi primera vez, y me dejo con ese vacío aun mas grande después de completar el final verdadero, por que si... Afterlife añade dos finales nuevos, uno de ellos el verdadero... y mereció la pena, todo lo añadido en historia eclipso todo lo malo que tenia con la actualización, podría contar todo lo que me gusto, pero esta es una de esas joyas que uno mismo debe quitarle el polvo y hacerlo parte de uno mismo. En mi caso el vacío que me dejo hizo que no lo jugara en años, me dejo tan satisfecho que volver a jugarlo seria solo por vicio, es una sensacion que solo unos pocos juegos han conseguido tener conmigo, y este lo ha conseguido dos veces.

La razón de mi reseña es porque cuando empecé a jugarlo de nuevo pensé en dejar una reseña diciendo que por favor jugarais la versión original ya que la Afterlife empeora un poco el principio, pero el juego me cerro la boca, demostró que cocinar lento merecía la pena, y aunque para mi siempre recordare el original con especial cariño, no puedo negar que Afterlife es realmente el juego en su versión final, lo que tenían pensado para este mismo pero que no pudieron hacer de primeras, lo cual solo enfatiza que el aspecto que menos me gustaba de la version es que cambiaban una obra de arte que me llego a tocar.

Dicho todo esto solo quiero que sepas que aunque en Steam pone un mensaje de que no esta disponible en Español de España el juegos si que lo esta, y si lees esto creo que todos los que nos hemos completado el final verdadero estamos de acuerdo en decir lo siguiente; -por favor, cuida bien de Sorun y por lo que mas quieras acaricia al perro.

It's missing some polishing in almost every aspect:
- Music is very good at times, but gets cut off a lot. There is a lot of unnecessary silence.
- Combat has some depth to it, but also has some awful hitboxes.
- Bosses have a decent variety of mechanics, but get very spongy in the second half of the game.
- Story has its moments, but forces itself way too much into the experience. Random cutscenes between boss attempts ruined the flow for me.

You need to pick a starting class in the first minutes of the game - which locks you into a skill tree that can either hard-carry your playthrough or do absolutely nothing useful. While the game is beatable with all of them, getting every achievement probably isn't. To avoid headaches, pick Soldier.

Weapons are very unbalanced. Most weapons scale of Finesse or Strength, offering nothing but damage. However, the great hammer scales of Vitality, allowing you to hit very hard very quickly while also being very tanky. Honestly, it's so broken that it's fun; it definitely shouldn't be changed. Would be nice if the rest of the weapons were equally broken. 

Also, there's an ARG boss in here that has you follow a 20 step guide on how to find, unlock and fight the guy. It's an innovative twist, gotta give it that much, but I hated the gameplay related to all this.

Потому что иди и гринди. Набивай валюту, качай уровни, качай шмотки. Я и не против, но локаций для этого нет. Потому что...
5. Ужасный дизайн уровней и карта. Всё по пути закрыто, куча ненужного бэктрекинга, а пометить его никак. Четверть всего времени прохождения просто бегал и искал, куда идти дальше.

Итог: абсолютно не стоит текущей стоимости в 941 рубля и потраченного времени даже для любителей жанра.

English:
One of the best Metroidvanias I've ever played. The story is simply masterful, incredibly profound, even prompting reflection on life and death. It boasts exceptional replayability, challenging you time and time again, and you can choose from numerous classes at the start of the game. While there are few weapons, each offers distinct advantages and abilities, and several possess attack types that exploit the weaknesses of various bosses and common enemies.

It's not a perfect game, as the boss fights, especially in Heroic mode, sometimes feel a bit uneven, or perhaps they were intentionally designed to be somewhat unfair. However, its strengths far outweigh its weaknesses. I highly recommend it. If you enjoy Soulsvanias that are beautiful, lengthy, challenging, feature an excellent story, a wealth of detail, and run on a potato computer, this is the game for you. I give it a solid 9 out of 10. This is a seriously underrated Metroidvania that deserves more fame. Believe me when I say it's worth buying at full price and you'll want to complete the game 100%.

It feels like there was a distinct quality difference in metroidvania soulslikes before and after Hollow Knight, with Death's Gambit being a relic of the past in unfortunate ways (both were in development around the same time).

Whether or not you like Hollow Knight, one of its biggest impacts to the indie game industry (imo at least) was proving that soulslikes could be just that: souls "likes" and not just try to be Dark Souls in 2D. But Death's Gambit has nothing going for it like that.

Best way for me to put it is this hearkens back to a time when devs who wanted to recreate the souls formula felt too restricted to perfectly translate the formula to 2D, and therefore ignored the strengths of this dimension and drops any semblance of a unique identity or polish.

It lacks modern resolution options, many basic QOL features and has all the worst traits of mimicking the early souls combat, story, and mechanics without understanding why it was like that and how to make it work. It's clunky and basic with unnecessary choices that do not benefit the design.

And then there's the Metroidvania aspects that the game doesn't seem mechanically built around to be enjoyable. It's not fun or interesting to move in the world. Unlike 3D souls that them even being Metroidvanias with interlocking paths is novel in itself, a 2D Metroidvania has to also be an engaging platformer to really nail the enjoyment.

It doesn't stand on its own as either a good souls or a 2D metroidvania game and especially not as a combination of the twom

Apparently this is a significantly improved version from the original release, but you can't put a coat of paint over a mediocre base and expect that to make it good.

You're better off with the now plethora of much better soulsvania titles that exist than to play this. Unless you really ran out of options and need to scratch that itch, I'd skip this one.

全実績取得したのでレビューします。
全実績取得したメトロイドヴァニアだと以下の順でオススメです。
ナインソール>ホロウナイト>デッドセルズ>シルクソング>ブラスフェマス2>デスガンビット>ENDER LILIES>ENDER MAGNOLIA>Ori and the Will of the Wisps

全体
微妙な翻訳とインタフェースのため、最初の印象は悪かったです。
ただシナリオがわかりやすく面白くどんでん返しもあるため、楽しめました。

システム
・回転攻撃
　回避直後の攻撃の事です。このゲームは回避攻撃が超重要です。
　回避中は無敵である事、回避攻撃は攻撃力が1.5倍である事、回避攻撃でバフが発生するスキルがあるため積極的に使うべきです。
・スキル/アビリティ
　アビリティの光の矢がとても強いです。スキルでモーション高速化できます。
　アビリティ名は光の矢ですがスキル名がピアッシングです。(翻訳が違うため、光の矢は使えないのかと勘違いしていました。)
　STR/INT系の装備でもFIN12まで上げて使いましょう。
・エッセンス/強化
　ダークマターと知識の実というアイテムが有限です。ニンジンで知識の実が交換できるため、ニンジンはダークマー弱点の書を交換した後は知識の実だけと交換しましょう。
　エッセンス稼ぎはウサギのNPCが復活するのでオススメです。魔術師に瞑想を依頼し、主人公が跪いた状態で数秒放置するとステータスの振り直しが出来ます。
　エッセンスを稼ぐ際は取得エッセンス増加をつけ、エッセンス増加のオーラもつければウサギ1回で2000以上稼げます。
　下位の強化石はショップで適当な装備を買って分解、上記の強化石はショップで買える鎧を10でクラフトできますのでエッセンスを稼げば強化出来ます。
　また、1週目は150レベルが上限です。
・ステ振り
　前述の光の矢のためFINは12まで振るべき。ダブルジャンプ→空中回避→ヒップドロップ→地上回避を行うために、スタミナも10くらいまで上げるのがオススメです。
　HPを上げることで羽の回復量が高まりますが、防具であがる分でHP強化は十分ですので、上記まで振ったら自分の武器にあったSTR/FIN/INTに極振りでOKです。

トロコンについて
・DLC
　たぶん必要です。私は購入しました。
　ただ、DLCではダークマターが無制限入手、ジャンプ無限化、攻撃20%増のオーラが取得できるためDLCの購入を進めます。
・エンディングは3つありますが、Cには実績がないので、トロコンをするならAかBを目指しましょう。
　ただし、弱点の書とボス討伐をコンプするにはAとB両方のルートに行く必要があるため、最低2週必要です。
　弱点の書はNewGame+でないと引き継げないのでNewGame+で二週目の後半まで進めないとロコン出来ません。
・パーフェクトランの実績
　Cルートで取得出来ました。
　下見をした後一回目のランで取得できました。長剣で3時間15分ほど。
　レベルがあげられないため、属性装備は付けれないので塔のゲートを開けるための3属性のアイテムを保持しておくのを忘れずに。
　火と雷は投擲物。闇はエンチャントで開錠しました。
・一番強いボス
　英雄Bルートボスが一番苦戦しました。100回ほどで撃破でき、一番面白かったです

I have given this game a chance two times - once on PS5 and once on my Steam Deck and sadly I can't recommend it. Let's start from good to bad.

Combat is good. It is is fluid and enjoyable. I can perhaps think of a few minor complaints, but overall it's the best part of the game. Extra points for no contact damage.

Difficulty curve and progression feel well thought out in the part of the game that I played.

Having different classes in the game is a great idea. Abilities are a bit of a hit and miss, some are interesting but others are way too niche, and the multiclsssing mechanic is a little bit useless. Overall still a good system that allows the classes to differ in gameplay.

Visuals are technically decent. And performance is good. No major bugs spotted.

Music exists and shows up to do its job. That's all I can say about it. Same for voice acting.

Art style and world design. We are hitting the bad now. The biomes feel randomly placed, the art style of the game is incoherent. One of the biomes feels like it belongs to a different game altogether. The boss designs are also hit and miss.

The level design feels annoying to traverse. It's the game where you miss the fast travel because of how bad the level design is. And this is not something you would want in a souls-vania game.

The writing. Ah, the bottom of the barrel. It's not just bad, it's atrocious. It's cringe worthy to the point of breaking the immersion. It's full of unsolicited millennial humour at the worst possible moments. It literally feels like Marvel Souls.

While I initially enjoyed the combat and the idea of engaging with it in different ways thanks to the class system I couldn't even finish the game once due to the off putting world and downright disastrous writing.

Maybe I'll give the game another chance later, but for now I unfortunately do not recommend it.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
Death's Gambit: Afterlife is a revised version of the original Death's Gambit which listened to player feedback & added a lot of new lategame content. This game is the absolute definition of 'what if you had dark souls except in 2D', it focuses heavily on combat and is master class in fight strategy and build/class versatility. Metroidvania elements are rather minor, but the world is mostly open with a power-up based progression that's fairly linear early on. The voice acting and story enrich the game like no other, the latter especially putting you up for a loop questioning the entire journey if you pay close attention to what's going on.

[u]Grade: 10/10[/u]

[h1]Story - A[/h1]
You play as Sorun, a man who died in an expedition to the immortal city of Aldwyn, but you made a contract with death to destroy the source of immortality and bring an end to the immortals' reign. The story seems simple at first and you get to know the motivations of Sorun, but as you discover more of the strange and disturbing things happening in this world, you're being set up for quite a wild ride that subverted even my expectations. Some shortcomings of the story have to be cohesion at times, since the world building can feel a bit all over the place.

[h1]Combat - S[/h1]
The build versatility is the best I've seen from any game; you can carefully craft your build with talents and strategize to beat a boss with a lot of different playstyles. Blocking stands central in this game, but you get a very satisfying feeling from parrying AND perfect blocking, which should become your bread and butter. The regular fights offer a good challenge to get you to learn the fight, and the heroic rematches offer a match more difficult experience with extra rewards. The boss fights range from amazing to mixed bags, but even those are satisfying to master in the late game. If you really like the combat, the DLC is absolutely worth it since it gives you an extra boss fight and several combat challenges, including a very difficult boss rush.

[h1]Art - A[/h1]
The game looks good and fits the setting, nothing too special, but there are absolutely some really cool visuals sprinkled in here from time to time.

[h1]Music - S[/h1]
The soundtrack is INSANELY memorable, I can't stress it enough how well the soundtrack is used and how it empowers so many moments/fights in this game. The leitmotif is sprinkled into a lot of songs, but in such a way where each song sounds unique, which is an amazing feat by the composer. Even if you don't play this game, give the soundtrack a listen, it's magnificent.

[h1]Quality of Life - C[/h1]
Unfortunately this is the main shortcoming of the game, you can feel the spaghetti code at times and its best played with mouse and keyboard. Some people have ran into issues/crashes, design/balacing isnt always on point, you can't remap specific controls, cycling through items can be awkward, etc. I do believe this is the main reason why this game isn't as well known, but you gotta look past it and settle for keyboard + mouse to get past most issues.

[h1]Gameplay - S[/h1]
The right balance of exploration, bossfights, checkpoints, punishment and story make the experience very fresh. There is a lot of lategame content where the game is at its best: a secret boss, the lategame heroics, DLC content, etc. I've never ever felt like things got stale in this game since it was so varied in its ideas.

[h1]Charm - SSS[/h1]
It's very clear the developers love games and wanted to make a game, it doesn't try to be perfect, it has some corny dialogue, it has some genuinly heartwarming moments.. You can just tell the developers wanted to pour their ideas into this and make something as a tribute to the franchise they liked, It makes the idea of this game so endearing. I can also easily tell that I wouldn't have loved this game as much if it wasn't for the afterlife content

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
This is a hidden gem: play it if you like 2D strategic-leaning soulslike combat with a touching story.
